boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Illinois traditions and recurring campus rituals, from Homecoming events to landmark lore and stadium performances.

cards.title: Illinois Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Weeklong alumni-and-campus celebration
cards.notes: Check the official schedule before heading out; the 2026 celebration runs September 27–October 3 and includes events across campus.
cards.short_summary: Illinois has held a multi-day Homecoming celebration since 1910.
cards.evidence_claim: University Archives identifies the 1910 Illinois event as an early multi-day Homecoming, while the official site lists the current annual weeklong celebration.
cards.access_notes: See the official schedule for event-specific locations, registration, and ticket requirements.

cards.title: Watch the fountain turn orange
cards.subtitle: Illinois Homecoming kickoff at Alice Campbell Alumni Center
cards.notes: Stop by the Alice Campbell Alumni Center during Homecoming kickoff to see the annual fountain dyeing and confirm timing on the event schedule.
cards.short_summary: Homecoming opens with the Alumni Center fountain dyed as part of the kickoff.
cards.evidence_claim: The official 2026 Homecoming page names the annual Alumni Center fountain dyeing as its Sunday kickoff event.
cards.access_notes: The official page says everyone is welcome to stop by; confirm the date and time for each year.

cards.title: Walk, roll, or run the Homecoming route
cards.subtitle: Anniversary Plaza to Alice Campbell Alumni Center
cards.notes: Use the posted Homecoming Run route from Anniversary Plaza to the Alumni Center; it is presented as a rain-or-shine walk, roll, jog, or run.
cards.short_summary: The annual Homecoming Run connects Anniversary Plaza and the Alumni Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The official 2026 Homecoming page invites participants to run, jog, walk, or roll from Anniversary Plaza to Alice Campbell Alumni Center.
cards.access_notes: Confirm event timing and any registration details on the official Homecoming site.

cards.title: Find a spot along the parade route
cards.subtitle: Kirby Avenue, Gregory Drive, and First Street
cards.notes: Check the annual route before you go; the 2026 parade starts at Kirby and Fourth, travels west on Gregory, then turns south on First.
cards.short_summary: A campus parade remains a recurring part of Illinois Homecoming.
cards.evidence_claim: The official 2026 Homecoming page lists an annual Homecoming Parade and specifies its route through campus.
cards.access_notes: Use the official Homecoming schedule for start time, route changes, and viewing guidance.

cards.title: See the orange-and-blue card section
cards.subtitle: Memorial Stadium student cheering tradition
cards.notes: At a home football game, watch the designated student section assemble card displays; the University Library traces the tradition back to 1910.
cards.short_summary: Block I grew from a 1910 pep club into a long-running Illinois cheering tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: University Library archives state that Block I began as a 1910 student pep club and that orange-and-blue cards were introduced in 1926.
cards.source_title: More than Just a Cheering Section: The Block I
cards.access_notes: Requires access to a home football game; follow stadium instructions for the card display.

cards.title: Follow the wooden turtle rivalry trophy
cards.subtitle: Illinois–Ohio State football tradition
cards.notes: Look for coverage around the Illinois–Ohio State game; the wooden turtle is exchanged as the rivalry trophy rather than a live animal.
cards.short_summary: Illibuck is the Illinois–Ohio State rivalry trophy, now represented by wood.
cards.evidence_claim: University Archives documents that Illibuck began as a live turtle and became a wooden replica after the turtle died in 1927.
cards.access_notes: The exchange is tied to the Illinois–Ohio State football rivalry; game attendance requirements vary.

cards.title: Join the Three in One singalong
cards.subtitle: Marching Illini halftime performance
cards.notes: At halftime, listen for “The Pride of the Illini,” “March of the Illini,” and “Hail to the Orange”; participants traditionally stand and sing.
cards.short_summary: The Three in One is a traditional Marching Illini halftime medley.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library’s music collection describes Three in One as the traditional Marching Illini halftime performance and identifies its three songs.
cards.access_notes: Typically experienced during a home football game; consult game-day programming for the performance.

cards.title: Take the graduation Alma Mater photo
cards.subtitle: Alma Mater statue near Green and Wright
cards.notes: Around graduation, plan ahead for a photo with the robed Alma Mater statue; campus staff note that lines can wrap around the block.
cards.short_summary: Graduates traditionally line up for a photo with Alma Mater in graduation attire.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois GradLIFE states that students traditionally have their photograph taken with Alma Mater while the statue wears orange-and-blue graduation robes.
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor landmark; graduation-period queues can be lengthy.

cards.title: Read the Eternal Flame’s disputed romance lore
cards.subtitle: Class of 1912 gift on the Main Quad
cards.notes: Visit the monument between Lincoln Hall and the English Building, but treat its eternal-love kiss story as campus lore rather than established fact.
cards.short_summary: The Eternal Flame’s romantic promise is a well-known but disputed Illinois legend.
cards.evidence_claim: The Daily Illini describes the Eternal Flame’s kiss-for-eternal-love story as a well-known but disputed myth and identifies it as the Class of 1912 gift.
cards.source_title: Burning question: Is Eternal Flame kiss of fate?
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus monument; no participation is required to appreciate the landmark and its lore.

cards.title: Spot the graduating-class gifts
cards.subtitle: Landmarks including Alma Mater, Altgeld Chimes, and Eternal Flame
cards.notes: Use campus walks to connect landmark plaques and histories: Illinois graduating classes gave works including Alma Mater, Altgeld chimes, and the Eternal Flame.
cards.short_summary: Graduating classes historically left physical gifts that became campus landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: The Daily Illini reports that Illinois class gifts include Alma Mater, the Altgeld chimes, the Eternal Flame, Illini Grove barbecue pits, and Illini Union furniture.
cards.source_title: Class gifts connect old alumni to new Illini
cards.access_notes: These are separate public campus landmarks; observe any building access rules at individual sites.

warnings: The supplied Admissions traditions URL was excluded as requested. Eternal Flame lore is explicitly labeled disputed.
